attributes.residual: REFUTATION FIRST: v2 concluded the frame had 'a FLOOR of 40 in our build that no declaration edit reduces ... a compiler-internal reservation not reachable from declarations'. THAT IS FALSE. Deleting ONE local - the single-use, immediately-dead `SndDesc44* dt` - and inlining its one expression took the frame 64 -> 56 and low_gap 40 -> 32, making the frame and all three (r1) slots (40/44/48) EXACTLY equal to target in one probe, with real 30 -> 14. v2's declaration probes removed the wrong locals. WHAT THE FRAME ACTUALLY COSTS, measured by four independent trades: `dt` and `rt` each cost 8 nominal bytes, while `q` and `bt` cost NOTHING (removing either left the frame at 64 unchanged) - they are fully registerized, so they cannot be spent as currency to buy room for another declaration. Scope does not help either: moving `rt` from the inner block to function scope did NOT free the low region (frame stayed 64), which measures claim.law.inner-block-pad-reaches-below-the-compiler-temps as NOT applicable to ordinary named pointers here - only declaration COUNT matters. THE RESULTING TENSION IS THE CAP, and it is exact and fully named: with BOTH dt and rt declared, the opcode multiset is IDENTICAL (123/123, 0t) and the only residual is the known association reorder - but the frame is 64 (8 too big, real 53). With only ONE of them declared, the frame is exactly 56 but the dropped pointer's accesses degrade from base+constant-displacement to indexed (dt dropped -> add/lha becomes addi/lhax; rt dropped -> add/lfs and add/stfs become addi/lfsx and addi/stfsx). There is no third local to spend, so exact-frame and exact-stream are mutually exclusive from source. Best retained = drop rt, keep dt: real 12, frame exact, 4 addressing rows plus the association reorder. NOT RETRIED (correctly veto'd by v2): the pointer-reassociation axis at @a8-bc, closed there at 3 forms; it survives here unchanged as a pure reorder (target add r31,r0,r12 + addi r31,r31,408 vs ours addi then add).
